ledger.note: 1581: Raghudev, Chilarai's son, splits the kingdom at Barnagar near the Manas and takes the eastern portion ('This division occurred in 1581'; infobox 'Established 1581'). He paid tribute to his uncle Nara Narayan until 1587, when 'Raghudev stopped paying tribute and declared himself independent'. The page describes the land as the north bank of the Brahmaputra between the Sankosh and the Bhareli, running south towards Mymensingh; it gives no area. The Barak Valley goes with the eastern portion as a bridge (koch-bihar's split event).

After 1596: Raghudev moves the capital from Barnagar to North Guwahati. The page gives no year, only 'Under these circumstances' after the events of 1596-1597; 1597, the year of the Koch Bihar-Mughal alliance's victory over him ('The Koch Bihar-Mughal alliance defeated Raghudev in May 1597'), is the bridge.

ledger.note: 1613: Koch Hajo ends in the Mughal conquest of Kamrup (infobox 'Mughal conquest of Kamrup 1613'; Parikshit Narayan, ruler 1603-1613, was sent to Delhi). The Mughals set up a sarkar and the Ahoms took the Barnadi-Bharali land (Darrang) as a vassal tract from 1615; the Bijni zamindari between the Sankosh and the Manas survived to 1864. The page gives no single end date.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 by sa-06-x. A state Cliopatria lacks: cliopatria_names empty, one new keyframe. Two pages opened (Koch Hajo, Koch dynasty); the Cooch Behar State and Kamata Kingdom pages opened for koch-bihar agree on the 1581/1587 dates. WebFetch returned extracts.

Dates: founded 1581 by Raghudev (Koch Hajo page infobox and text; the Koch dynasty page has his rule over the territory beginning 1581); independent in 1587 on Nara Narayan's death (both pages; the Cooch Behar State page dates the split to 1586, which the Koch Hajo page does not give). The end is not a single date on the page: the infobox has the Mughal conquest of Kamrup in 1613, the Koch dynasty page has the land occupied by the end of 1612, the text has Parikshit driven to Pandu in 1614 and 'within three decades' of the split. 1613 is used at confidence 2.

Page silent / not drawn: the area; the territory south of Rangamati lost to Isa Khan (before 1594, no year); Parikshit's occupation of Bahirbandh from Koch Bihar (between 1603 and 1608); the Darrang tract installed under Balinarayan as an Ahom vassal (1615 on the Koch dynasty page, no year on the Koch Hajo page); the Ahom reoccupation of Kamrup in 1657-1667 and the Mughal loss of it in 1682 (the land after 1613 belongs to the Mughal and Ahom dossiers). The Barak Valley is drawn with the eastern portion because Raghudev was Chilarai's son and no page says otherwise; neither Koch page names it after 1562.

Cross-dossier: koch-bihar (split 1581; vassal pair 1581-1587 recorded there as the suzerain), mughal-empire (successor; its ledger should carry the 1613 gain), ahom-kingdom. The Raghudev reign 1581-1603 is shown to 1602 and Parikshit Narayan's 1603-1613. Gazetteer: Barnagar and the Sankosh, Manas and Barnadi rivers are absent; the shape uses discs at 90.6 E 26.2 N (70 km) and 91.6 E 26.2 N (60 km), minus the Cooch Behar disc, and the Barak Valley disc (92.65 E 24.75 N, 60 km).
